mechanism: Both drugs can cause fluid retention and peripheral edema through different mechanisms, with sacubitril enhancing natriuretic peptide effects and pioglitazone promoting sodium/fluid reabsorption via PPAR-γ agonism, increasing risk of decompensated heart failure.
action: Monitor closely for signs of fluid retention and worsening heart failure; assess need for diuretic adjustment; consider pioglitazone contraindication in patients with NYHA Class III-IV heart failure or recent acute decompensation.
